<div class="learn-box">
**What you will learn**

Select records, set inclusive time windows, and reduce them to first, last, count, ever, closest, any and all values.
</div>

This chapter uses the public synthetic Synthea27Nj numeric connection from [Getting started](book-00-start.html).

**You need:** the packages and helpers from [Getting started](book-00-start.html#before-you-start).
Run the sections in order in a fresh R session in your `book-work` directory.

## Start this chapter

Start a fresh R session in the `book-work` directory created in
[Getting started](book-00-start.html#get-the-book-helpers). Run this setup first:


``` r
library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R")
practice <- book_connect("numeric")
conns <- practice$conns
```

The connection is ready; `conns` identifies the server used by the analysis calls.

## Define the records once

[Chapter 4](book-04-vocabulary.html) identifies Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in
Blood as **3000963** and gram per deciliter as **8713**.
An *event* describes which records the server should read. These simulated hemoglobin measurements
have numeric values recorded in grams per deciliter (g/dL). Concept IDs here are vocabulary inputs;
they are not patient identifiers.


``` r
measure <- omop_event("measurement", concepts = 3000963L,
  value = "value_as_number", unit = omop_unit(8713L))
```

The unit declaration accepts g/dL values; other units become missing unless
you declare a conversion. It also records the unit of the result.
Use an `omop_unit()` conversion when your study needs conversion.

## Set a public time window

A *window* is an inclusive range of days around an *anchor*, the reference date.
A fixed date works even when the population has no index event.


``` r
history <- omop_window(NULL, NULL)
lookback <- omop_window(-365, 0, anchor = "2020-01-01")
```

`history` includes all recorded dates. `lookback` includes only the 365 days
before 2020-01-01 and that date itself. We will compare the two after extraction.
An omitted window on an advanced reducer reads all history; a simple-layer
shortcut usually defaults to history through the index. Choose explicitly.

## First and last values

A *reducer* turns many records into one value per person or episode.


``` r
first <- omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("first_value", window = history))
last <- omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", window = history))
```

These select by date, source and record key, not by the size of the value.
By default they skip missing values. `missing = "keep"` chooses the row first,
so the selected row can give a missing value. With no records, both give `NA`.

## Mean values

A mean uses all nonmissing numeric values in the window. It answers a different
question from choosing the first or last recorded value.


``` r
mean_value <- omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("mean", window = history))
```

The unit is still g/dL. Do not average numeric concept IDs or mixed units.

## Count and ever


``` r
n <- omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("count", window = history, distinct = "day"))
ever <- omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("binary", window = history))
```

Count measures distinct measurement days here; `distinct = "row"` counts records.
Ever is 1 when any record exists and 0 otherwise. Neither requires a nonmissing
numeric value. In a defined empty window both count and ever are zero.

## Any and all test the values


``` r
any_high <- omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("any", window = history,
    predicate = omop_where(value >= 16)))
all_high <- omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("all", window = history,
    predicate = omop_where(value >= 14)))
```

Ever tests whether a record exists. Any and all test a condition on its values.
Here any asks about readings at least 16 g/dL; all asks whether every reading is
at least 14 g/dL. Both are arbitrary teaching cutoffs, not clinical reference limits.
A missing value makes its comparison unknown; a true value settles any, and a
false value settles all. Otherwise an unknown remains missing. Empty windows
give any = 0 and all = NA: without measurements there is no all-value result.
This differs from R's `all(logical(0))`, which is TRUE.

## Assign the columns privately


``` r
reducers <- omop_recipe(variables = list(first = first, last = last,
  mean = mean_value, days = n, ever = ever, any_high = any_high, all_high = all_high),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
recipe_execute(reducers, out = c(people = "D_reducers"), conns = conns)
```

The columns are now in `D_reducers` on the server. Request one approved
aggregate at a time:


``` r
book_summary("D_reducers$first", datasources = conns)
```



|Site |Statistic | Value| N valid| N missing|

|site |5%        | 11.29|      28|         0|
|site |10%       | 12.48|      28|         0|
|site |25%       | 12.97|      28|         0|
|site |50%       | 13.70|      28|         0|
|site |75%       | 15.43|      28|         0|
|site |90%       | 16.19|      28|         0|
|site |95%       | 16.86|      28|         0|
|site |Mean      | 13.99|      28|         0|

All 28 people have a first nonmissing measurement. Their mean is 13.99 g/dL;
this gives each person one observation regardless of how often they were tested.

``` r
book_summary("D_reducers$last", datasources = conns)
```



|Site |Statistic | Value| N valid| N missing|

|site |5%        | 12.34|      28|         0|

The last readings average 14.89 g/dL across the same 28 people. First and last
can coincide for someone with only one reading.

``` r
book_summary("D_reducers$days", datasources = conns)
```

|Site |Statistic | Value| N valid| N missing|

The mean is 3.86 measurement days per person, with a median of 4. A frequency table of each
exact count is withheld on this dataset because some nonzero cells are below
`nfilter.tab` (3); the entire table is withheld, not just its small cells.
The summary describes the distribution of measurement frequency without listing
all exact count frequencies. See the table refusal once:


``` r
day_table <- dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_reducers$days", useNA = "no", datasources = conns)
day_table$validity.message
```

```
#> [1] "All studies failed for reasons identified below"
```

The message withholds the table. It does not say that these people have no measurements.


``` r
ever_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_reducers$ever", useNA = "no", datasources = conns)
book_counts(ever_result)
```



|Category | Count|
|:--------|-----:|
|1        |    28|

Everyone in this public dataset has a hemoglobin measurement. A person without
one would have ever = 0 in this defined window.


``` r
any_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_reducers$any_high", useNA = "always", datasources = conns)
book_counts(any_result)
```



|Category | Count|
|:--------|-----:|
|0        |     9|
|1        |    19|
|NA       |     0|

The released counts show 19 people with at least one reading at or above 16 g/dL
and 9 without one. A known qualifying measurement is enough for any, even
alongside an unknown value.


``` r
all_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_reducers$all_high", useNA = "always", datasources = conns)
book_counts(all_result)
```



|Category | Count|
|:--------|-----:|
|0        |    24|
|1        |     4|
|NA       |     0|

Four people have all readings at or above 14 g/dL; 24 do not.
All distinguishes unknown comparisons from an empty set of records.

``` r
book_summary("D_reducers$mean", datasources = conns)
```



|Site |Statistic | Value| N valid| N missing|

|site |5%        | 12.90|      28|         0|

The mean of the 28 person-level means is 14.47 g/dL. Averaging all measurement

## Restrict the last value to one year


``` r
recent <- omop_recipe(variables = list(last = omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", window = lookback))))
recipe_execute(recent, out = "D_recent", conns = conns)
recent_mean <- dsBaseClient::ds.mean("D_recent$last", type = "combine", datasources = conns)
recent_missing <- dsBaseClient::ds.numNA("D_recent$last", datasources = conns)
data.frame(Mean_g_dL = recent_mean$Global.Mean[1, "EstimatedMean"],
  N_missing = recent_missing$site)
```



| Mean_g_dL| N_missing|
|---------:|---------:|
|     14.85|        24|

The mean is 14.85 g/dL, but 24 of the 28 people have no reading in this year.
Only four contribute, compared with all 28 in the all-history summary. We show
a mean rather than quantiles for this small group. People without a recent
reading remain in the roster with missing values.

## Value at the index

The `omop_study()` shortcut combines an index event, variables and outputs in
one recipe. Let the first hemoglobin measurement set the anchor for each person. *Value at index*
means closest within a chosen tolerance; it need not occur on the index day.


``` r
at_index <- omop_study(measure, outputs = "baseline",
  baseline = list(hemoglobin = omop_value_at_index("measurement", 3000963L,
    tolerance = c(-30, 0), unit = 8713L)))
recipe_execute(at_index, out = c(baseline = "D_at_index"), conns = conns)
```

The tolerance excludes later measurements. The shortcut uses `closest_value`;
its default tolerance would include 90 days before and 30 days after.


``` r
book_summary("D_at_index$hemoglobin", datasources = conns)
```



|Site |Statistic | Value| N valid| N missing|
|:----|:---------|-----:|-------:|---------:|
|site |5%        | 11.29|      28|         0|
|site |10%       | 12.48|      28|         0|
|site |25%       | 12.97|      28|         0|
|site |50%       | 13.70|      28|         0|
|site |75%       | 15.43|      28|         0|
|site |90%       | 16.19|      28|         0|
|site |95%       | 16.86|      28|         0|
|site |Mean      | 13.99|      28|         0|

The mean is again 13.99 g/dL: because the index is the first hemoglobin reading,
the closest value in [-30, 0] is that same reading. This equality follows from
the chosen index; an index such as a diagnosis need not coincide with a lab.
Only people with an eligible hemoglobin measurement enter this indexed study. If a required anchor is missing,
a window is undefined and every reducer gives `NA`, including count and ever.

## Convert to a common unit before reducing

A unit declaration alone keeps values already in that unit and makes other units'
values missing; an explicit conversion normalises them before the reducer runs.
This example converts g/dL to g/L, multiplying by ten. These are the vocabulary
names for the input and target units:


``` r
units <- ds.omop.concept.lookup(c(8713L, 8636L), conns = conns)
units$pooled[c("concept_id", "concept_name")]
```



| concept_id|concept_name       |
|----------:|:------------------|
|       8713|gram per deciliter |
|       8636|gram per liter     |

Concept 8636 is gram per liter; 8713 is gram per deciliter. The conversion
below changes the unit by multiplying by ten.


``` r
lab_gl <- omop_event("measurement", 3000963L,
  unit = omop_unit(8636L, convert = list("8713" = c(factor = 10, offset = 0))))
```

Rows already in g/L retain their value. Other undeclared units become missing by
default; they are not guessed. A declared conversion also transforms reference
ranges. Use the same target and conversion map across sites before pooling.


``` r
converted <- omop_recipe(variables = list(mean_gl = omop_variable(event = lab_gl,
  reducer = omop_reduce("mean"))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
recipe_execute(converted, out = c(people = "D_converted"), conns = conns)
```


``` r
book_summary("D_converted$mean_gl", datasources = conns)
```



|Site |Statistic |  Value| N valid| N missing|
|:----|:---------|------:|-------:|---------:|
|site |5%        | 129.05|      28|         0|
|site |10%       | 131.47|      28|         0|
|site |25%       | 137.85|      28|         0|
|site |50%       | 143.25|      28|         0|
|site |75%       | 153.35|      28|         0|
|site |90%       | 157.00|      28|         0|
|site |95%       | 159.24|      28|         0|
|site |Mean      | 144.67|      28|         0|

The overall mean is 144.67 g/L, ten times 14.47 g/dL. This run uses the dataset's unchanged
recorded units; it does not pretend that the source already had mixed units.

## Value bins and explicit high/low flags

A *bin* groups numeric values into a declared interval. These cutoffs are arbitrary
teaching choices, **not clinical reference ranges or treatment thresholds**.
We apply them to each person's mean, privately.


``` r
mean_value <- omop_variable(event = measure, reducer = omop_reduce("mean"))
band_levels <- c("below 14", "14 to below 15", "15 or above")
binned <- omop_recipe(variables = list(mean = mean_value,
  band = omop_number_bins(mean_value, breaks = c(-Inf, 14, 15, Inf), labels = band_levels),
  high = omop_number_flag(mean_value, "ge", 15),
  low = omop_number_flag(mean_value, "lt", 14)))
recipe_execute(binned, out = c(output = "D_lab_bins"), conns = conns)
```

The band is an ordered factor directly on the server. Its order matters for
model contrasts.


``` r
bins_result <- dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_lab_bins$band", useNA = "always", datasources = conns)
bin_display <- book_counts(bins_result)
bin_display$Category <- ordered(bin_display$Category, levels = band_levels)
bin_display[order(bin_display$Category, na.last = TRUE), ]
```



|Category       | Count|
|:--------------|-----:|
|below 14       |     9|
|14 to below 15 |     9|
|15 or above    |    10|
|NA             |     0|

There are 9 people below 14, 9 from 14 to below 15, and 10 at or above 15 g/dL.
All nonzero cells meet the release threshold. You see
the checked counts, never the private rows. A different set of bins can cause
the entire table to be withheld; a refusal is not an empty or zero table.
The left boundary is included and the right boundary excluded in these bins.


``` r
book_counts(dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_lab_bins$high",
  useNA = "no", datasources = conns))
```



|Category | Count|
|:--------|-----:|
|0        |    18|
|1        |    10|

The high flag is 1 for the same 10 people in the top band and 0 for the other 18.
The ungrouped mean column remains available for numeric analysis.

`abnormal_high` and `abnormal_low` reducers compare each measurement with its
recorded reference bounds. These hemoglobin data have no such bounds, so their
zero comparable-abnormal counts would not establish normality. Study-defined
flags are a different, explicitly chosen definition.

## Try it

Add a count of measurement rows and compare its released mean and quantiles
with the measurement-day summary above.

<details><summary>Solution</summary>


``` r
row_count <- omop_recipe(variables = list(rows = omop_variable(event = measure,
  reducer = omop_reduce("count", window = history, distinct = "row"))),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
recipe_execute(row_count, out = c(people = "D_row_count"), conns = conns)
book_summary("D_row_count$rows", datasources = conns)
```



|Site |Statistic | Value| N valid| N missing|
|:----|:---------|-----:|-------:|---------:|
|site |5%        |  1.00|      28|         0|
|site |10%       |  1.70|      28|         0|
|site |25%       |  3.00|      28|         0|
|site |50%       |  4.00|      28|         0|
|site |75%       |  4.00|      28|         0|
|site |90%       |  5.00|      28|         0|
|site |95%       |  5.65|      28|         0|
|site |Mean      |  3.86|      28|         0|

The row and day summaries are identical here because nobody has two hemoglobin
records on the same day. With duplicates, row counts would count each record
while day counts would count that date once.

</details>

## Another numeric exercise

Build a variable using `omop_number_change()` to calculate last minus first
for people with at least two readings. Is this the same quantity as a slope?

<details><summary>Solution</summary>


``` r
change_recipe <- omop_recipe(variables = list(change = omop_number_change(measure)))
recipe_execute(change_recipe, out = c(output = "D_event_change"), conns = conns)
book_summary("D_event_change$change", datasources = conns)
```



|Site |Statistic | Value| N valid| N missing|
|:----|:---------|-----:|-------:|---------:|
|site |5%        | -2.94|      25|         3|
|site |10%       | -2.58|      25|         3|
|site |25%       | -1.40|      25|         3|
|site |50%       |  1.60|      25|         3|
|site |75%       |  2.40|      25|         3|
|site |90%       |  3.20|      25|         3|
|site |95%       |  3.76|      25|         3|
|site |Mean      |  1.02|      25|         3|

The mean change is 1.016 g/dL among 25 people; 3 are missing because they have
only one reading. It differs from 14.893 − 13.986 = 0.907 because those two means
include all 28 people. Change is in g/dL, without dividing by elapsed time. Native change needs
two eligible readings; a single reading stays missing rather than becoming zero. A fitted slope uses
all eligible dates and values and has units per day. Continue with
[Working with lab values](book-14-labs.html) for both methods and pooled analyses.

</details>

## Recap

An event chooses records, a window chooses time, and a reducer answers one question. Empty records and an undefined anchor are different.

**Next:** [7. Populations and index events](book-07-populations.html).
